title: JSON Mode: attenuated-token repair playbook and decoder fidelity heatmap
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Empirically map and mitigate a class of partial-stream 'attenuated token' failures where strict JSON mode enters an unrecoverable decoding state for long-running streams. Deliver a reproducible heatmap of failure modes across model families, sequence lengths, temperatures and prefix-caching states, and codify a repair/rollback playbook that productizes graceful fallback behavior and alerting. This ticket focuses on test harnesses, telemetry, and an ops playbook rather than runtime kernel changes.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible harness that can replay 1000+ streaming sessions and categorize JSON-mode failures into at least four root-cause buckets (early truncation, token corruption, interleaved tool token leakage, decoder deadlock)
A failure heatmap visualizing failure frequency vs (model, max_seq, temperature, batching level, prefix-cache-hit) exported to the Console experiment dashboard
A written repair playbook with step-by-step operator commands (canary reroute, relax-jsonmode flag, resend last-k tokens, queued fallback) and automated runbook links in SLO alert messages
Automated smoke tests that verify fallback flows (relax-jsonmode -> constrained-decoder-retry -> rollback-to-nonstream) pass in CI for two representative models
Telemetry hooks that emit structured failure events (failure_bucket, sequence_position, truncated_bytes, last_emitted_fragment) and are captured by existing runtime-telemetry plumbing
tasks: Design replay harness and failure taxonomy (owner: Daniel)
Implement streaming session recorder that captures raw token stream, alignments, and KV-cache hints (owner: Priya Shah)
Run large-batch experiments across: Llama-2 variants, Mistral, and a curated open-turn-based chat model (owner: infra-experiments)
Create Console experiment dashboard to visualize heatmaps and session samples (owner: Console team)
Draft operator repair playbook and integrate with PagerDuty alert templates (owner: SRE)
Write CI smoke tests for fallback flows and add to release gating (owner: QA)
Postmortem template and long-term mitigation proposals for runtime/language-model teams (owner: Aisha)
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Kumar: Created ticket after on-call incident where strict JSON mode never recovered and customer had silent errors. Initial hypothesis: prolonged low-entropy token sequences cause decoder to enter an internal 'dead' state when streaming partial JSON fragments.

2026-03-03 - Daniel Park: Prototype recorder implemented that samples raw token streams and captures last-emit offsets. Early runs (n=200) show correlation between high-prefix-cache-hit and increased truncation events for some quantized kernels.
2026-03-05 - Priya Shah: Added KV-cache hint capture into recorder. Found a reproducible case with a 512->8192 token transition that repeatedly triggers constrained-decoder deadlock on model X.

2026-03-07 - Console team: Dashboard skeleton created; we need a stable export schema for heatmap tiles (suggested fields: model, seq_bucket, temp_bucket, batch_size, cache_hit_rate, failure_bucket_count).
2026-03-09 - SRE (Luis Ortega): Drafted PagerDuty message template that includes a one-click runbook link and an automated flag to reroute affected traffic to 'non-strict-json' fallback pool.

2026-03-10 - Aisha Kumar: Running extended experiments (n=2k sessions). Early result: enabling a 'soft-accept' window of last-8 tokens before hard json-assert reduces observed unrecoverable failures by ~65% for one model family. Need QA verification before proposing as default behavior.
notes: This ticket explicitly avoids kernel-level fixes (left for follow-ups) and instead targets observable, testable mitigations and operator procedures that can ship within a minor runtime release.
Keep the heatmap and raw session captures available to model-onboarding team for targeted model-specific remediation proposals.
Consider adding a 'relax-jsonmode' query parameter for canary traffic to validate repair efficacy with limited customer impact.
